label: COUNTS-ONLY amendment v2 (2026-10-31): tensor-contraction IC (ic.tensor_contraction_v1, m = 2) against rho.negation and the prime IC baseline on the registered bench-roster prime curves of 10, 12 and 14 bits (counted S only, no wall time)
description: Supersedes, for counted S only, docs/ecbench/specs/tensor-ic-vs-rho.json (left frozen and unchanged; measurement there: rounds 6, warmup 1, order alternate, L2, timeout_seconds 900). Same curves, targets (target_seed 20261030, 8 per curve), arms, arm methods, measurement seed 20261030 and per-execution timeout. Only measurement changes. Gate-forced change: isolation_required L2 to L0. On EKS the run-ecbench L2 gate grades any solve under 1 ms as L1 (record.rs MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3) and exits 42, and rho at 10-16 bits solves in microseconds (run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 records L1); L0 is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts. Discretionary changes, filed before any data (protocol v2): rounds 6 to 1 (S is a deterministic function of (workload, algorithm seed) and replays exactly, so a repeated seed adds nothing; rounds 2-6 would add new walk seeds per target, i.e. power, which P1 does not need; cost: C3 (tensor vs ic-mitm) is probably underpowered, so no_ranking is the expected outcome there, not parity); warmup 1 to 0 (a warm-up only absorbs one-time wall costs, which counted S does not see; with warmup 0 the measured round uses absolute seed index 0, which no measured round of the original used); order alternate to alternate_measured (with warmup 0 and one round both orders run the single round in spec order, so the plan order is identical; alternate_measured matches the 16-bit original and avoids ecbench's warning that alternate parity counts warm-ups). timeout_seconds is a wall-clock limit (runner.rs): at L0 whether a row ends verified or timeout depends on the host; a timeout row is host censoring (unknown), never a negative result. No wall-time figure from this session is a result. Caveat: on 64-bit builds lambda <= 64, root_u = lambda/131072 = 0 and public inputs take the finite-size fallback; nothing here exercises the recursive subexponential kernel; ic.tensor_contraction_v1 is an exponential toy (protocol H1). Protocol: research/hashed_ecdl_counts_20261031/protocol.json (v2).
